title: Fresh-database sign-up works first time (first report's 500 on first Create account is fixed)
steps: 1. On the fresh copy, Create an account. 2. Fill lightkeeper_rue, email, password twice. 3. Create account.
expected: Account created, straight into the Chapter Hub
actual: Exactly that, first try, no 500 and no 'connection dropped' flash when the new campaign desk opened (both happened in the first playtest). Username rule text under the box is clear.

title: 'Invite player' on a brand-new campaign reads like the way to bring players in, but it is only for bringing a player back
where: Lightkeeper's desk, Roster, under Join Requests, laptop 1440x900
steps: 1. Create a new campaign (no players yet). 2. Under 'No one waiting to join', open Invite player.
expected: On a fresh campaign, either hide it until someone has played, or label it 'Invite a player back' and point new players to the campaign code (e.g. 'New players join with the code lantern-ward').
actual: A text button 'Invite player' sits right where a new Lightkeeper looks for how to invite her group. Opening it says 'The player rejoins with a new investigator, without waiting for your approval' (rejoins? nobody has joined yet). Typing a stranger's name gives a clear alert 'No player found with that username.' (good). Source comment (InvitePlayer.jsx) confirms it is meant 'once in a blue moon' to bring a player back. Nothing on the Join Requests area tells the Lightkeeper to share the campaign code.

title: Dispatch and End Assignment stamps sit just below the fold at 1440x900 with no hint the left column scrolls
steps: 1. Open a new campaign's desk. 2. Look for the Dispatch button.
expected: The Dispatch stamp visible without scrolling, or a visible cue that the left column scrolls
actual: The dispatch slip ends with the text box; the Dispatch stamp is at y=769 of a 761-high page. The left column does scroll on its own (mouse wheel over it; the first report's 'inner scrolling for side columns' fix works, praise), but there is no scrollbar or fade to say so. A Lightkeeper typing her first dispatch has to guess where the send button is. Folding the four section tabs into a row would free about 170px.

title: Timer events now reach the Activity Log, and the screen-reader status clears with the timer (first report #7 and #42 fixed)
steps: 1. Switch Timer on. 2. Set 0:05, Start. 3. Let it run out. 4. Clear.
expected: Log lines for set/start/clear, live status that does not go stale
actual: Log shows 'set the timer to 0:05', 'started the timer (0:05 left)', 'cleared the timer'. The live region said 'Timer started.', then 'Time's up.', and is empty after Clear (first report #42 said it kept saying Time's up). Focus lands in the minutes box after Clear, ready for the next one. Small nit: no log line when time runs out, so a player who glanced away cannot tell from the log that the countdown ended.

title: Lightkeeper Resources editor: text is double-spaced off the ruled lines and touches the left edge; tab shows an unexplained '(1)'
where: Lightkeeper's desk, Notebook, Lightkeeper Resources tab, laptop 1440x900
steps: 1. Notebook > Lightkeeper Resources. 2. Type a few lines of notes (one per line).
expected: One line of text per ruled line, a little inner margin, and a tab label that says what any count means
actual: Each typed line takes two rules (56px per line on 28px ruling), so the text floats between the lines rather than on them; the first letters sit flush against the box's left border (no padding). Autosave works well ('Saved' with a tick within a second). After saving, the tab reads 'LIGHTKEEPER RESOURCES (1)', with no hint what the 1 counts (one page? one unread?).

title: Unsent dispatch draft (location and text) is wiped by visiting Circle, Notebook or Map
where: Lightkeeper's desk, dispatch slip (Roster section), laptop 1440x900
steps: 1. On the Roster section, type a Location ('Wick Street, Hollin Cross') and some dispatch text, do not press Dispatch. 2. Click Map (or Notebook, or Circle) in Desk sections. 3. Click Roster again.
expected: The draft is still there, as the Lightkeeper Resources notes are (they autosave). A GM drafting a dispatch often checks the map or her notes mid-sentence.
actual: Location and 'Your dispatch' come back empty (0 / 2000), with no warning. Seen twice: once after Notebook > Map > Circle > Roster, once after Map > Roster. No console errors. Cause (read in source): SceneManager.jsx:147-149 keeps location/atmosphere/ownText in component state seeded from the circle's last SENT dispatch, so the unmounted Roster section drops the draft. The Own words/Template toggle is remembered (readMode), the draft is not. Fix: keep the draft in the store or sessionStorage per campaign.

title: Pass Notes: '@Circle (everyone)' and '@Environment (shown to everyone)' read as the same thing; the picker's options sit outside the Pass Notes region for a screen reader
where: Lightkeeper's desk, Pass Notes 'To:' picker, laptop 1440x900
steps: 1. Roster section, Pass Notes. 2. Open the 'To:' picker.
expected: Labels that say what differs, e.g. '@Circle: a note from you to everyone' and '@Environment: narration, shown in capitals with no name'; options announced as a list belonging to the 'To:' control
actual: Both say everyone. Only the source (ActivityLog.jsx, type 'environment') shows that Environment posts an unsigned bold capitals line, i.e. scene narration. The options appear in the accessibility outline as two loose buttons after the page's last status, not as options of the picker; the toggle is a button whose name changes '▼' to '▲' (the arrow is read out).

title: Map is a single fixed picture of the Fairelands: no way to pin or mark where the assignment is
steps: 1. Desk sections > Map.
expected: A way for the Lightkeeper to drop a pin or label (e.g. Hollin Cross, the dispatch location) that players see on their Map, or to upload a scene map
actual: The rulebook map shows, crisp and well framed, with 'Open full size' and a proper alt text 'The Fairelands'. That is all: our campaign's borough (Hollin Cross) is not on it, and the dispatch location is not tied to it. Fine for flavour, not a tool I can run a scene with.

title: [long-name-overflow] On a phone the leading circle name collapses to one letter per line and its 'leading' tag is cut off
where: Circle Formation Papers, II. Name the Circle, suggested names list (CircleCreationPopup.jsx:336-350), phone 390x844
steps: 1. Formation table, four players. 2. Bram (phone 390x844) suggests 'The Ninth Night'; another player suggests 'the ninth night' (merges, 'suggested 2 times'). 3. Two players vote for it and two for another name (2-2 tie, so it shows 'leading'). 4. Look at its row on Bram's phone.
expected: The name reads on one or two lines and its tags (yours, suggested 2 times, count, leading) wrap or fit inside the row, as before the long-name fix.
actual: The tags are shrink-0 and take the whole row, and the name span (now min-w-0 with overflow-wrap:anywhere) shrinks to 0 px wide: 'The Ninth Night' is drawn one letter per line (364 px tall), and the tags run 53 px past the row so 'leading' shows as 'lea' (at 360 px wide they run 101 px past it, off the screen). The 80-character Z name on a 360 phone is 85 px wide and 280 px tall. The fix for long names (min-w-0 + overflow-wrap:anywhere on the span, tags left shrink-0 in one row) caused it; at 820 and 1366 the rows are fine.

title: [report-questions-tally] The tally's Add N Illumination is live again in a second tab or on another device, so the same reports can be added twice
where: Lightkeeper Circle page, Illumination Questions paper (gm/CirclePage.jsx addTally; illumTallies kept only in the browser's localStorage)
steps: 1. Reports open, one player files a report with a key (tally: Keys some, +2). 2. Lightkeeper at 1440x900 opens the Circle page in tab A, then the same desk in tab B (B takes the socket). 3. In tab B tick a question and press Add N Illumination: the paper says 'Added N Illumination'. 4. Back in tab A press 'Use this tab': the paper still shows 'ADD N ILLUMINATION'; press it. 5. Also: open the Lightkeeper's desk in a fresh browser (another device) after the Add.
expected: Once an assignment's tally has been added, every Lightkeeper desk shows 'Added N Illumination' (the fix proposed storing it once on the circle), so the reports cannot be counted twice.
actual: Tab A added again: illumination went 0 -> 2 (tab B) -> 5 (tab A), log 'The Ninth Night gains 3 Illumination (2 to 5).' and 'milestone 3 reached!'. A fresh browser after the Add shows a live 'ADD 2 ILLUMINATION' with Total +2. The 'added' flag and the question ticks live in illumTallies in localStorage, not on the circle, so another tab already open or another device does not know the reports were counted. This is the same early-advancement harm the first report described, by another route.

title: [lk-formation-status-thin] The Lightkeeper's relationship ticks say 'has proposed one' for a player who proposed three
where: Lightkeeper's desk, Circle formation so far, VI. Relationships (CircleFormationStatus.jsx:240), laptop 1440x900
steps: 1. Formation table with four players. 2. Bram proposes to Iris, Cassandra and Dev; Dev proposes to Iris and Cassandra. 3. Open the Lightkeeper's desk and read VI. Relationships.
expected: Each player's line says how many they have proposed, or of how many (e.g. 'proposed 3 of 3'), so the Lightkeeper can see who still owes a proposal.
actual: 'PROPOSED: Bram Ashby, has proposed one ... Dev Okafor, has proposed one' although Bram proposed three and Dev two; the tick only means 'at least one'. The line above also reads 'Waiting for an answer from Iris Ashe (2 relationships), Bram Ashby and Cassandra Wilhelmina Fairweather-Montgomery (2 relationships)', where the last count can be read as shared by Bram and Cassandra.

steps: 1. Bram Holt's desk on a phone 390x844, Circle tab, Illumination at 5. 2. Look at the gold-ringed pips 3, 6, 9, 12. 3. Read the report form. 4. On the Lightkeeper's desk add Illumination past 3 and read the log.

Below, tick the keys you fulfilled.'), but nothing on the player's form says what a key is worth (only the Lightkeeper's tally does).
